# E0321: refutable pattern

This pattern can fail to match, so the code needs a way out: write `let Some(n) = name else return …`, or use `match` or `if let`.

- Rule: [`patterns.irrefutable-positions`](../../reference/09-patterns.md#patterns.irrefutable-positions)
- Reported at: the pattern.
- Tier: `core`, checked in the `types` phase

## Example

This program makes the mistake:

```stilt E0321:2
fn first_name(name: Option<str>) -> str {
  let Some(n) = name
  n
}
```

This one is fixed:

```stilt
fn first_name(name: Option<str>) -> str {
  let Some(n) = name else return "nobody"
  n
}
```

## What the compiler prints

`stilt check` on [`E0321_else_inside_a_try.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0321_else_inside_a_try.lt):

```text
── REFUTABLE PATTERN ─────────────────── E0321_else_inside_a_try.lt:7:7  [E0321]

This pattern can fail to match: the `else` is part of the operand of `try`, so
this isn't a let-else:

  7 │   let Some(n) = try cell(text) else raise "missing"
    │       ^^^^^^^

This pattern can fail to match, so the code needs a way out: write `let Some(n)
= name else return …`, or use `match` or `if let`.

To fix it, put the `try` in parentheses:

  7 │   let Some(n) = (try cell(text)) else raise "missing"
    │                 +              +
```

`stilt check` on [`E0321_refutable_pattern.lt`](../../tests/diagnostics/E0321_refutable_pattern.lt):

```text

This pattern can fail to match, which isn't allowed here:

  2 │   let Some(n) = name
    │       ^^^^^^^

This pattern can fail to match, so the code needs a way out: write `let Some(n)
= name else return …`, or use `match` or `if let`.
```
